newsitem.title: FRANCE: Forex options hit Remy 1996/97 results.
newsitem.headline: Forex options hit Remy 1996/97 results.

text.p: French drinks company Remy Cointreau said on Wednesday an exceptional loss of 101 million francs ($17 million) for 1996/97 year results stemmed from a 158 million franc loss on currency options.

The group posted a net profit of 36 million francs for the year to March 31, 1997, down from 120 million in the previous year. It made provisions of 277 million francs for restructuring costs and potential future losses.
It reported an exceptional profit of 176 million francs from asset sales and financial operations. It also made a two million franc foreign exchange loss.
The stock was down 8.13 percent at 136.8 francs at 1228 GMT. The stock market had expected profit after exceptionals between 120 and 135 million francs.
Taking these elements into account, "the weakness in the group's results is deceptive," chairman Heriard Dubreuil said. He added that there would not be significant provisions in the coming years.
Remy made an exceptional profit of 76 million francs in 1995/96 and foreign exchange gain of 34 million.
Pre-tax pre-exceptional profit rose to 97 million francs versus 39 million, after two years of declines.
"The 1996/97 year marks a period of transition. We have given ourselves the means to build solid and sustainable growth which is already visible in the 1997/98 year," Dubreuil said.

The group saw turnover increase for all its brands, except for cognac, which was hit by sales declines in Japan and Taiwan. It expects efforts to cut costs in these two countries will bear results in the 1997/98 year.
The group expects margins to improve on cognac and on liqueurs, spirits and champagne. ($ = 5.936 French Francs)
